Rivian Prepares Spoken Waze and Google Maps Alerts, Alternative Routes, and More in Upcoming Update
6 photos
Photo: Rivian
Having delivered the highly appreciated Halloween Update, Rivian is already busy testing the software features that will roll out soon with the 2026.41 update. Among the highlights are navigation upgrades such as alternative routes, audio alerts for Waze and Google Maps, as well as configurable state of charge at the destination.
For those sad that Tesla might give up its entire vehicle lineup soon, rest assured, Rivian might offer just the right EV for you and your family. Rivian has been no slouch in software features, and its vehicles have been highly appreciated. There's a good chance that, should Tesla decide cars are no longer fashionable, Rivian will replace it as the EV carmaker of choice.
This has been even more obvious after the EV startup launched the R2 crossover. On the software front, the Halloween update has shown Rivian on equal footing with Tesla in software features . Rivian Assistant has also been appreciated as a much better companion than Grok in Tesla EVs, although the gap narrowed with the latest Tesla updates.
One area where Rivian appears to get ahead of Elon Musk's company is the navigation system. Rivian has been adding new features like there's no tomorrow, while Tesla has been mostly stagnant. Routing errors have annoyed even Tesla's most faithful, and the carmaker has finally conceded that an overhaul is in order to plug the holes in the navigation.
Rivian not only has a much better route planner, but has refined the navigation system by integrating Waze alerts, including speed cameras and police reports. Now, Rivian is preparing to add new features with the 2026.41 update, which is due later this month. Among them are alternative routes, spoken Waze and Google Maps alerts, and the ability to set the desired state of charge at the destination or at charging stops.
The latter has already been included with the A Better Route Planner (ABRP) app, which underpins Rivian's navigation and route planner after it was bought by Rivian. It provides more options to drivers on winter road trips and those who tow a trailer. Setting a comfortable battery buffer can alleviate range anxiety and ensure peace of mind that you'll get to a charger with enough battery charge.
As for the spoken Waze and Google Maps alerts, they can make a difference. These alerts were already offered in Rivian vehicles with the 2026.31 update , but only as visual cues. You still had to glance at the screen to see police or speed cameras ahead, and there was a good chance to miss these alerts. Now that they are spoken out loud, it's less likely to miss them while driving.
The navigation also provides more alerts than before, including for road incidents, lane closures, and objects on the road. Even better, the navigation now displays traffic signs and stop signs on the map. These improvements make Rivian Navigation good enough that owners might not decry the lack of Apple CarPlay and Android Auto support. Big Navigation upgrades coming to Rivian R1 and R2 with the 2026.41 OTA: ⚡️ Alternative routes ⚡️ Audio for Waze and Google Maps alerts ⚡️ More alerts: road incidents, lane closures, objects on the road ⚡️ Traffic signs and stop signs on the map ⚡️ Configurable arrival charge at charging stops and destination — Wassym Bensaid (@WassymBensaid) November 9, 2026
